question: How much additional therapeutic exposure does CereVasc obtain per unit of added device complexity, manufacturing burden and clinical risk?

added_complexity.device: Size-selective membrane or coating in eShunt drug delivery lumen
added_complexity.manufacturing: Membrane integration + QC (moderate — ePTFE is standard material)
added_complexity.clinical_risk: Membrane fouling (addressed by fail-safe), drug-lumen occlusion (drainage preserved)
added_complexity.regulatory: Combination product (device + drug); adds to CereVasc's existing combination product pathway

exposure_per_complexity: 288.4% exposure improvement for moderate device complexity. RETENTION-ONLY is the most efficient architecture (highest exposure per unit complexity). Combined adds separation complexity but only incremental exposure.
economic_proposition: Existing CereVasc platform → controlled exposure platform. The incremental value: pharma partners can achieve predictable tissue exposure with lower dose, fewer administrations, and broader therapeutic class coverage. CereVasc transforms from 'access provider' to 'exposure controller.'

classification.economic_proposition: HYPOTHESIS — depends on physical validation and pharma partner interest
classification.cerevasc_strategy: EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE — CereVasc publicly seeks pharma partners
